title: Observation reads can trigger fontification hooks

environment.system_features: ACL GMP GNUTLS LIBSELINUX LIBXML2 MODULES NATIVE_COMP NOTIFY INOTIFY PDUMPER SECCOMP SQLITE3 THREADS TREE_SITTER ZLIB

mechanism: `buffer-substring' and `buffer-substring-no-properties' are different observation operations; the former can run `buffer-access-fontify-functions'.
hypothesis: Reading text with properties should invoke `buffer-access-fontify-functions', while `buffer-substring-no-properties' should not invoke the access fontification hook.
minimal_fixture: One temporary buffer with a buffer-local `buffer-access-fontify-functions' hook.
predicted_behavior: `buffer-substring-no-properties' returns text without triggering the hook; `buffer-substring' triggers it for the accessed range.

independent_checks.name: no-properties read did not invoke fontification

counterexample: A read-only observer that uses the wrong text API can load or compute display-derived state while claiming to be passive.
derived_gym_requirement: Observation APIs must be classified as passive state reads, derived inspections, or active diagnostics, and probe traces must record which class was used.
